_comment: Playwright MCP config — Khalid runs three monitors (laptop / Dell / Samsung), so a
fixed --viewport-size is wrong: the page would be letter-boxed at one size no matter
which screen the window opens on.
`viewport: null` is the official opt-out. Playwright docs (docs/src/api/params.md):
«Use null to disable the consistent viewport emulation ... making the viewport
depend on the host window size defined by the operating system.»
«no_viewport: Does not enforce fixed viewport, allows resizing window in headed mode.»
Result: the page always fills the real Edge window on whichever screen it lands on,
and it scrolls exactly when the content genuinely does not fit.
--- BLACK SCREENSHOTS AFTER SCROLLING (measured 19 Aug 2026) ---
Symptom: on a long page, a viewport screenshot taken after a programmatic scroll came
back solid black. Measured on a 16,701px article page, same page, same session:
scroll 0        viewport shot  197 KB   renders
scroll 5,000    viewport shot   73 KB   only the top ~400px rendered, rest black
scroll 14,100   viewport shot  8.5 KB   fully black
element shot deep in the page   3.1 KB  fully black
fullPage: true                1.76 MB  renders the whole document
Two theories were tested and DISPROVED, so nobody re-tests them:
1. Paint race — double requestAnimationFrame + 600ms before capture: still black.
2. Emulated viewport larger than the real window — shrinking the emulated viewport
BELOW the real window size (1333x622 inside a 1280x672 window): still black.
What it actually is: the GPU compositor does not re-rasterise the scrolled region for
the capture. `--disable-gpu` forces software rasterisation, which renders the whole
scrollable area deterministically. `launchOptions.args` is the only way to pass browser
flags here — playwright-mcp has no CLI flag for it (verified in its README options
table, Context7 /microsoft/playwright-mcp).
Workaround with no reload needed: take screenshots with `fullPage: true`. It uses a
different capture path and was measured working on the same page (1.76 MB above).
launchOptions.args --auto-open-devtools-for-tabs: opens DevTools automatically for
every tab (Chromium/Edge flag) so the Network panel is visible during live tests.
Add it back when you want that; it is off by default because it shrinks the render area.
Changing this file (or .mcp.json) needs a Claude Code reload — MCP reads config at startup.
